::: {.section-card}
### Source representativeness: Pracuj.pl vs MRPiPS / PUP

**Pracuj.pl** provides a conservative lower bound on online vacancies. The vacancy estimator codes empty fields as one position, explicit counts at face value, and “multiple positions” without a number as two.

**MRPiPS administrative data** capture vacancies reported by employers to poviat labour offices (PUP). The two sources reflect **different market segments**, not different measurements of the same population:

- Pracuj.pl dominates **white-collar, IT, and specialist** hiring.
- PUP reporting over-represents **blue-collar, public-sector, and foreign-worker** vacancies; private employers have no general obligation to report online vacancies to PUP.

Pracuj.pl is therefore treated as a strong proxy for **market-driven labour demand**. A seasonal drop in PUP vacancies from H1 to H2 may partly reflect cyclical hiring and activation programmes concentrated in the first half of the year.

```{=html}
<div class="chart-block">
  <div class="figure-caption-title"><strong>Figure 6.</strong> Vacancy structure by KZiS major group: Pracuj.pl vs MRPiPS / PUP (2025, share of total)</div>
  <div id="chart-kzis-comparison" class="plotly-chart plotly-chart--wide" role="img" aria-label="Comparison of vacancy shares by KZiS major group between Pracuj.pl and MRPiPS PUP data in 2025"></div>
  <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> The figure highlights selection differences between private online recruitment and public labour-office reporting. Pracuj.pl better captures market-driven, white-collar and specialist hiring, while PUP data better captures public-sector, blue-collar, and some foreign-worker vacancies.</p>
</div>
<p class="notes source-note">Source: Pracuj.pl job postings mapped to KZiS via title embedding; MRPiPS / PUP vacancy reports for H1 and H2 2025 (<a class="paper-link" href="https://psz.praca.gov.pl/-/bezrobotni-i-wolne-miejsca-pracy-wg-zawodow-i-specjalnosci-w-2025-r." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">MPRiPS</a>).</p>
```
:::

::: {.section-card}
### Baza Usług Rozwojowych (BUR)

BUR is Poland’s largest national registry of training and advisory services, launched in 2016 under the EU Partnership Agreement and operated by PARP. The analysis is restricted to **training services** (`Usługa szkoleniowa`).

The registry includes diverse provider types — private companies, NGOs, public educational institutions, and public-finance entities — and, as of April 2025, **75% of registered providers** offered services with public co-financing. From January 2026, registration in BUR is a mandatory prerequisite for providers delivering publicly funded training (EU funds and the National Training Fund).

**Analytical scope.** Skill-mismatch analysis compares **2025** BUR listings with 2025 job postings. Earlier BUR years are retained separately to trace how subsidised supply — for example in care services — evolved over funding cycles.

The full database contains **~870k training-service editions (2016–2025)** and **~131k in 2025**. Annual volumes reflect EU funding cycles (2014–2020 vs 2021–2027), pandemic disruption, and the system’s early ramp-up — not training needs alone. Analyses therefore work with **within-year skill shares** to reduce sensitivity to these volume swings.

::: {.stat-grid}
```{=html}
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">Training services (2025)</p><p class="stat-value">~131k</p></article>
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">Registered providers (2025)</p><p class="stat-value">~3,100 active</p></article>
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">Full registry (2016–2025)</p><p class="stat-value">~870k</p></article>
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">Public co-financing</p><p class="stat-value">75% of providers</p></article>
```
:::
:::

::: {.section-card}
### Training providers in BUR (2025)

In 2025, roughly **3,100 providers** delivered training through BUR — about half of all entities registered on the platform. Providers were classified by keywords in legal names (e.g. *Sp. z o.o.* / *S.A.* → private company; *uniwersytet* / *politechnika* → public education; *fundacja* / *stowarzyszenie* → NGO).

::: {.section-card}
### Course recurrence in BUR

BUR assigns a fresh `id` to every edition of a service, so raw posting counts cannot reveal whether the catalogue is genuinely new each year.

**Strict “same course” key.** Two postings are treated as the same course only if they share all four attributes: `provider_id`, normalised title (lowercased, diacritics stripped, edition/format markers removed), rounded number of hours, and `kategoria_uslugi`. A course is **recurring** if its key appears in ≥2 calendar years (2016–2025).

::: {.stat-grid}
```{=html}
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">Unique courses (2016–2025)</p><p class="stat-value" id="recur-unique-courses">274,081</p></article>
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">Recurring courses</p><p class="stat-value" id="recur-recurring-courses">42,549</p><p class="stat-sub">15.5% of unique courses</p></article>
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">Postings on recurring courses</p><p class="stat-value" id="recur-recurring-postings">418,785</p><p class="stat-sub">48.3% of all postings</p></article>
<article class="stat-card"><p class="stat-label">2025 postings re-running earlier courses</p><p class="stat-value" id="recur-2025">38,130</p><p class="stat-sub">29.1% of 2025 postings</p></article>
```
:::

About half of BUR postings replicate an earlier offering by the same provider under the strict matching rule above.

```{=html}
<div class="chart-block">
  <div class="figure-caption-title"><strong>Figure 8.</strong> BUR postings by number of years a course remained on offer (2016–2025)</div>
  <div id="chart-bur-recurrence" class="plotly-chart plotly-chart--wide" role="img" aria-label="Distribution of BUR postings by number of years a course was offered"></div>
  <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> A substantial share of BUR postings are recurring offerings rather than entirely new courses. This points to stability in the training catalogue, but also raises questions about how quickly provision adapts to emerging skill demand.</p>
</div>
<p class="notes source-note"><strong>Posting (edition):</strong> one BUR row — a single edition with its own date, location, and price. <strong>Course:</strong> editions sharing provider, normalised title, hours, and category. <strong>Recurring course:</strong> a course appearing in ≥2 calendar years.</p>
```
:::

::: {.section-card}
### Recognised qualifications in BUR (until 2023)

Until 2023, BUR distinguished four types of **recognised qualifications** in the `inne_kwalifikacje` questionnaire:

- **Q1** — vocational qualification (craftsman / master / KKZ)
- **Q2** — state or public-authority qualification (e.g. UDT, Welding Institute)
- **Q3** — position-based entitlement after validation (e.g. excavator operator)
- **Q4** — international certificate from an identified list

From 2024, the form structure changed; Q1–Q4 fields are no longer populated in the same way. The chart below shows the historical composition through 2023.

```{=html}
<div class="chart-block">
  <div class="figure-caption-title"><strong>Figure 9.</strong> Share of BUR trainings ending with each recognised-qualification type (2016–2023)</div>
  <div id="chart-bur-qualifications" class="plotly-chart plotly-chart--wide" role="img" aria-label="Historical share of BUR trainings by recognised qualification type"></div>
  <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> Historically, recognised qualifications in BUR were distributed across several formal categories. Because the questionnaire changed after 2023, the figure is best used to understand the earlier qualification regime rather than current certification patterns.</p>
</div>
```
:::

::: {.section-card}
### Training completion documents (2025)

In 2025, BUR records whether a training ends with a formal competence certificate based on learning outcomes (**Q17–Q19**):

- **Q17** — document contains a description of learning outcomes
- **Q18** — validation carried out against criteria defined in learning outcomes
- **Q19** — separation of the training process from the validation process

A training is classified as ending with a **recognised competence certificate** only when all three conditions are met.

```{=html}
<div class="chart-block">
  <div class="figure-caption-title"><strong>Figure 10.</strong> Type of document issued by BUR trainings (2025)</div>
  <div id="chart-bur-documents-2025" class="plotly-chart plotly-chart--wide" role="img" aria-label="Share of BUR trainings by completion document type in 2025"></div>
  <p class="figure-interpretation"><strong>Interpretation.</strong> Most trainings with parsable metadata end with a recognised competence certificate. This indicates that BUR provision is often linked to formalised learning outcomes, although certificate quality and labour-market recognition may still vary.</p>
</div>
<p class="notes source-note">In 2025, 77.5% of training services with parsable qualification metadata end with a recognised competence certificate (Q17–Q19); the remainder issue an informal or attendance certificate only.</p>
```
:::
